what: The header of the prompt corpus published as an API: the version a project freezes. Declared BY HAND, for the same reason as the gate catalogue (gates/catalog.json): a project starts and finishes with the same version of the method, so what it froze has to read back the same two years from now.

version_scheme.note: The recipe -- canonical form, algorithm, encoding, and the rule that raises the version -- is declared once, there, and the build uses the same implementation. This file only says which keys the hash covers here, because the payload is a different one. One copy of each text.

changelog.changed: First DECLARED version of the corpus. The prompts themselves did not change: not one character of prompt text is touched here (D-049). What changes is the identity of what is published and the truth of what it declares. Identity: until now the only identifier was a git sha, which a build computes before saving and which therefore always names the change BEFORE the one that contains it -- useless as something to freeze. From here the version is declared by hand and the file carries a content hash the consumer RECOMPUTES, exactly like the gate catalogue. Truth: the file said language `en` while steps[].title carried the Spanish titles of the contracts; the titles now come from the English contracts (docs/en/peldanos/), which is where tool data belongs (D-051), so the declaration is true instead of approximately true. The file stays UTF-8 and is not ASCII: the prompt text is published verbatim, typographic punctuation included.
